races.name: Jack Frost Chiller & Freezer Hire Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Character Testing
runners_data.note: Top weight on OR 94 but has solid placed form over 16-17f on Good ground and is 18 days fresh; the tongue-tie is a positive signifier and Jamie Hamilton's big-race experience suits a messy finish.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: OR 91 for Jim and Suzi Best, 47 days off the track is the slight concern, but three placed efforts on Soft/Standard suggest versatility and Richie McLernon is a shrewd reader of pace in big fields.

runners_data.name: Colinski
runners_data.note: Four-year-old on OR 93 with the 3lb claim from Charlie Maggs potentially decisive in a tight finish; his two most recent runs show improved form over 16f on Good, and his previous win came on similar ground.

runners_data.name: Daring To Dream
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from seven runs on Good or Good-adjacent ground, but has been without a win in this run of form; genuinely suited to closing from well off the pace, though this congested field may see him operating slightly closer to the action than ideal.

runners_data.name: Louie The Legend
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with youth on his side but a modest string of finishes, including a third over 16f on Good; Tabitha Worsley rides and the horse has shown enough late energy to gate-crash if the pace collapses entirely.

runners_data.name: Karthala
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with four placed efforts from five runs over 16f on Good — arguably the steadiest form profile in the race; Sean Quinlan is the standout jockey booking and Jennie Candlish's 4/21 in the past fortnight indicates a yard in form, though his natural position is deeper than this map implies.

runners_data.name: Giddyupadingdong
runners_data.note: Won over this 16f trip on Good and has a habit of running on without quite getting to the front; Neil Mulholland's infrequent runners carry quiet confidence, and his 0.92 style-fit rating reflects that he will want to be further back than midfield shows.

runners_data.name: Rapid Mission
runners_data.note: 95 days absent is a notable absence flag and Tom Lacey's one win from five recent runners tempers confidence; he won over 20f on Soft and drops in trip/distance profile here, though he was placed on Good over the longer trip — treat as one for future reference.

runners_data.name: Brenda Lady
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a top-level booking for a horse rated just 79 and trained by David Rees on a small string; only three career runs recorded but placed in both efforts on Good ground, and the booking alone demands attention in a wide-open sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Battle Stride
runners_data.note: 242-day absence is the longest in the field and the fade-in-finish flag is a genuine concern; Richard Armson's yard is 0/0 in the past fortnight so this is purely a fitness question mark, and the heavy weight reduces the upside even if fit.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Fade-in-finish flag alongside a pattern of double-figure finishes on Soft; six previous runs suggest he handles Good better than soft, but Sam England's 1/4 recent strike rate offers little encouragement and the low OR limits his ceiling.

runners_data.name: Lady Fortune
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 20f on Good and drops back to 2m here — the trip shortening is an unknown but her recent winning form is the freshest in the field; Isabelle Ryder is a 5lb claimer so the weight relief is real, though consistency has been patchy over the longer trips.

runners_data.name: Granny B
runners_data.note: Lowest rated runner at OR 73 but carries form of four placed efforts from 15 Good-ground starts — never winning but rarely disgracing; Kevin Brogan takes over the ride and the horse's headgear (hood history) is worth watching, though this looks one run too many for a maiden at this level.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field, this race lacks any natural pace-setter prepared to dictate from the front, and the opening scramble is likely to produce a slow, scrappy gallop before the field compresses into a bunched sprint to the line over the final two flights. Every runner carries a hold-up profile, meaning those who can travel smoothly in mid-division and quicken late — rather than grind from the rear — hold the tactical edge. Character Testing, Golden Circet, and Colinski sit at the top of the weights and rate the most fluid movers through the pack, while Karthala and Daring To Dream are genuine hold-up operators mapped to midfield only because this field is saturated with closers who cannot all sit last. The race shape strongly favours horses with a late, fluent turn of foot who can find a clear passage in a tight sprint finish, rather than front-runners or wide-margin grinders. This field contains more pace-holding types than the map can accommodate — Karthala, Daring To Dream, Giddyupadingdong, Rapid Mission, and Brenda Lady are true hold-up horses displaced to midfield, and it is the lighter-weighted, fresher representatives among them most likely to secure their preferred position near the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bunched Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls along and converges into a tight driving finish off the last hurdle, favouring those with the sharpest late acceleration.
scenarios.body: With no pace to stretch the field, the race collapses into a cavalry charge up the run-in, rewarding any runner able to find a clear line and pick up quickly under pressure; Karthala's consistent placed form over this course distance and Colinski's recent hurdling experience make them well-suited to winning a tight finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strongest Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate fractions race still tests stamina on the testing Good ground, eliminating those who lack the engine to grind out 2m.
scenarios.body: A race that appears slow in the early stages can still produce a stamina test if the pace picks up sharply two out, catching out horses who are merely quick rather than genuine finishers; Character Testing and Golden Circet, both with creditable form over 16-17f trips on similar ground, are best equipped to see it out fully.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Shrewd Ride Wins It
scenarios.trigger: If a well-placed jockey executes a patient mid-division ride and produces their mount perfectly between the last two hurdles.
scenarios.body: In a field where nearly every horse wants to close from off the pace, the rider who finds the cleanest route through traffic and commits earliest to the drive will have a decisive advantage; Sean Quinlan on Karthala has the course craft to find that gap, and Lady Fortune's recent win form gives her handler grounds to hope Isabelle Ryder can produce a similar effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Gate-Crashes
scenarios.trigger: If an unconsidered runner — such as Louie The Legend or Brenda Lady — gets an uncontested position and pings the final hurdle to score at a big price.
scenarios.body: In a field this undifferentiated for pace, an unexpected front position or a clean round of jumping can allow a horse to steal the race before the closers organise themselves; Louie The Legend and Brenda Lady both sit on attractive marks and carry jockeys with nothing to lose tactically.

watchPoints.text: Karthala and Colinski are the two runners with the clearest combination of consistent placed form, top jockey bookings, and suitable ground history — if either gets a clear run between the last two hurdles, they are the most dangerous finishers in the race.

Lady Fortune drops back sharply in trip from her recent win over 20f; if the 2m distance proves too sharp, she could fade out of contention having travelled prominently, exposing backers at a potentially short price.
Battle Stride has not run for 242 days and carries the fade-in-finish flag — watch for any signs of laboured jumping before the home turn that would indicate the long absence has left its mark.

Sean Bowen's booking for Brenda Lady (OR 79, David Rees yard) is a market intelligence flag — if money appears for her in the ring before the off, the booking makes more sense than the bare form suggests.

Karthala, Daring To Dream, Giddyupadingdong, Rapid Mission, and Brenda Lady are all genuine closers forced into midfield by sheer weight of numbers — watch the traffic situation turning for home, as any interference in this group could ruin several winning chances simultaneously.

races.name: Bravo Benefits Celebrations Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with the clearest lead in the pace map; Harry Cobden's booking adds class to the seat, though OR 135 at the top of the weights is a significant burden over 3m and his five-run form string (045-43) shows no recent wins, with limited form on Good ground (0W2P in similar going).

runners_data.name: La Pinsonniere
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson's six-year-old arrives on 33 days' rest with consistent placed efforts at trips up to 26f, and the hg flag (tongue-tie/hood) suggests the yard have something to correct — Good ground is her medium and five placings in similar conditions (0W5P) paint her as a nearly horse who needs everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow
runners_data.note: A genuinely prominent-type racer who has won three of his last four outings, but this race has more prominent horses than positions available and he is the one most likely displaced into a midfield role that doesn't suit; Dan Skelton, booking Harry Skelton and running on just 8 days' rest, clearly targets this race seriously — the tp headgear is retained and his Good-ground record (5W7P) is strong.

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: The only natural hold-up horse in the field, ridden by claimer Beau Morgan (5lb), and his recent form (88-415) is patchy with wins at 23f on Good — in a small-field novice chase where the pace is likely to be controlled rather than searching, he needs the leaders to capitulate rather than his own latent ability to surface.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill is the lone confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and should lead from the outset at a measured, uncontested gallop over three miles of Uttoxeter fences. La Pinsonniere and Sunray Shadow are both genuine prominent types competing for the same ground behind the leader, meaning one or both will be forced wider or deeper than their natural position — Sunray Shadow, despite strong recent form, is most likely to be the one shuffled back given the redistribution mapping. Samuel Spade is the sole natural hold-up horse and will be content to track proceedings from the rear before making a bid in the closing stages. With Sony Bill dictating a sustainable pace and no rival likely to fire up an early battle, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-mid-profile runners who can sit comfortably just off the front and pounce in the home straight — the true hold-up horse faces a difficult test if the pace is not testing enough to stretch the field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Sony Bill is near-certain to lead, La Pinsonniere is best placed to sit second, and Sunray Shadow is most likely to be the one forced to accommodate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sony Bill Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill dictates an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front and no rival applies meaningful pressure at any stage.
scenarios.body: Sony Bill, rated OR 135 and suited to front-running, sets a comfortable gallop that never turns into a true test of stamina, allowing the leader to dictate every yard; La Pinsonniere, likely to slot in second, is the biggest beneficiary if she can travel smoothly and produce a clean jump at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If La Pinsonniere and Sunray Shadow both attempt to assert a prominent position early, creating an unplanned pace duel behind Sony Bill.
scenarios.body: A competitive surge into the prominent berths forces a faster-than-expected tempo, stringing the field out and turning this into a stamina test; Samuel Spade, tracking from off the pace, could pick up the pieces if front-runners empty.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sunray Shadow Marches Through
scenarios.trigger: If Sunray Shadow, despite being mapped to midfield, asserts his natural prominent position and travels powerfully to challenge Sony Bill before the last.
scenarios.body: Sunray Shadow's recent winning sequence — three from four — suggests he has the ability to overcome a suboptimal position if given daylight, and if his jumping holds up over the longer 3m trip he could challenge for the lead turning in; his trainer Dan Skelton is 4/27 in the last 14 days, suggesting in-form handling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Steal It Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final mile through jumping errors or fatigue among the leaders, handing Samuel Spade a rare opportunity to mop up.
scenarios.body: Samuel Spade has shown he can win from off the pace — his OR 124 win came at 23f — but his hold-up style is vulnerable in a small, slowly-run field where the pace rarely dries up sufficiently; Beau Morgan's 5lb claim could help, but the scenario demands the front rank to fold, which is an unlikely outcome when Sony Bill controls the tempo.

watchPoints.text: Sony Bill is the confirmed pace-setter and if he makes a jumping error early or is taken on by La Pinsonniere approaching the first, the race shape collapses entirely — monitor his jumping from fence one.

Sunray Shadow's redistribution is key: watch the first two furlongs to see whether Harry Skelton asserts to claim his natural prominent position or settles tamely into midfield, as that determines which scenario activates.

La Pinsonniere's headgear flag (hg:p) and the 33-day break for a Henderson runner in a small novice chase suggest a specific prep — watch for her to be ridden with confidence rather than conservatively, which could disrupt the pace hierarchy.

Samuel Spade's Beau Morgan claim (5lbs) reduces his 153lb burden but the hold-up style in a four-runner field is a structural disadvantage — watch whether Morgan rides him closer than expected to compensate for the small-field dynamics.

races.name: Sun Racing The Favourite Pullout Every Day Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Romany Brown
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner whose OR-115 ability on good ground gives her every chance of controlling this from the off; 254 days off the track is the key query, but her sim-going record of 8/9 is excellent and Ben Case has placed her well historically — if she retains her form, stealing this from the front is a live possibility.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy teams up with Jack Jones whose 2/13 in 14-day runners is a note of caution, but An Bradan Feasa's own form record of consistent placing on good ground at this trip (three wins, six places from 15 similar-going runs) makes her the most credible danger to the leader — a prominent racer who will likely sit second and pounce.

runners_data.name: King Ulanda
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor is a strong booking for Oliver Greenall and Josh Guerriero, and the horse's win over 18f on good suggests the trip is within range; a prominent-style runner who has shown inconsistency (PF6-14 recent form) and the tongue-tie is noted — a quiet jumper on the day could see him involved late.

runners_data.name: Machete Beach
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (3-1-1-3) and a top sim-going record, but by nature a front-runner who cannot get his preferred position in this shape — Gavin Sheehan will face an early decision about whether to fight for space or settle in behind, and either compromise will likely blunt this horse's most dangerous form.

runners_data.name: Ip Up
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse fitted with a hood, Sean Quinlan will settle this one at the back and ride for a late run; the horse's win on good over 16f last time out is directly relevant to today's conditions, and if the pace stays steady through the middle section this profile is the natural beneficiary.

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a high-class jockey and the Olly Murphy yard has a live 3/16 14-day record, but Ask A Sainte is a natural prominent racer who has been pushed back to midfield on the map — the horse's best form comes when bowling along in front, not chasing, which makes today's shape structurally awkward for a win challenge.

runners_data.name: St Just In Time
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's runner wears a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up type, but the sim-going record of 0 wins and 1 place from 4 runs on good is limited encouragement; Paul O'Brien will look to produce this horse late but the form figures on today's surface make it hard to project a winning performance.

races.paceDynamic: Romany Brown is the confirmed lone pace-setter and will stride straight to the front from the off, establishing a sustainable rhythm on good ground over this 2m trip — with no horse likely to push hard into that position, the pace will be honest rather than gruelling. An Bradan Feasa and King Ulanda are the next two prominent types who will press into the early positions just behind, creating a small lead group but not a true pressure cooker. This field carries more prominent-biased horses than the shape can accommodate: Machete Beach and Ask A Sainte are genuine front-runners by nature but are displaced to a midfield map position, meaning they will either have to work hard early to recover their preferred spot or race against their instincts — either outcome is likely to compromise them. The race shape favours a hold-up horse with a strong finishing kick who can sit quietly off an uncontested, metronomic gallop and produce a run from the back of the small field, or alternatively a prominent horse with the stamina to match Romany Brown's rhythm through the race and outsprint them home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Romany Brown Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Romany Brown leads from flag to finish without serious pressure and sets a gallop the field cannot adequately counter late.
scenarios.body: Romany Brown controls every yard of the race, exploiting the absence of any genuine challenger to the lead and conserving energy through the middle section; the prominent horses behind lack the gears to close the gap if she has been allowed a soft lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough to set up a finisher and a true hold-up runner produces a sustained run from the back of the field.
scenarios.body: Ip Up or St Just In Time sits last or second-last, bides their time off the steady tempo, and produces a run from the final flight when the front-runners have given their all; the uncontested early pace ultimately suits a fresh closer rather than the tired leaders.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Turns Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If An Bradan Feasa or King Ulanda moves up aggressively to challenge Romany Brown before the home turn, injecting real pressure into proceedings.
scenarios.body: A contested pace unravels the front group and the race becomes a test of class and jumping accuracy through the final two hurdles; a prominent horse with strong recent form and a live trainer angle capitalises as the lead group tires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Displaced Frontrunners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach or Ask A Sainte successfully forces their way to the front early despite their redistributed map position, turning this into a genuinely contested pace.
scenarios.body: Either horse burns energy recovering their natural front-running role, but if they succeed in leading from Romany Brown they could dictate on their own terms; however, the physical cost of that early effort on good ground over 2m makes this a low-probability and high-risk shape.

watchPoints.text: Machete Beach and Ask A Sainte are both natural front-runners likely to push early for a prominent position — watch the first two furlongs for traffic and potential interference as they compete with Romany Brown, An Bradan Feasa and King Ulanda for limited early real estate.

Romany Brown has been off the track for 254 days; if she shows any signs of ring rust at her hurdles in the early part of the race, the lead she is expected to establish could be vulnerable far sooner than her talent suggests it should be.

Ip Up's hood (headgear) is worth monitoring at the start — if the horse is fractious or slow away it will compromise the hold-up plan entirely and leave Sean Quinlan with too much to do at this 2m trip.

King Ulanda's recent form string (PF6-14) includes a fall and a pulled-up, meaning his jumping reliability is a live question in a 7-runner field — a jumping error from a prominent position could materially change the complexion of the race for every horse behind him.

St Just In Time steps up markedly in trip from its most recent runs over 11f at Stalls — the 2m hurdles distance today is nearly double its last two starts and fitness over this stamina test is an open question that Paul O'Brien will need to manage carefully in the pace shape.

races.name: Alfie Flatt 18th Birthday Celebration Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Theonlywayiswessex
runners_data.note: Confirmed lone front-runner with a strong record in similar good-ground chases (11 from 15 on sim going, two wins) and 42 days since last run looks straightforward; Alan King's eight-year-old can dictate entirely unopposed here, which is a major structural advantage, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a minor note given it is arguably racing closer to its natural position than others.

runners_data.name: Pep Talking
runners_data.note: Consistent good-ground performer (12 from 15, five wins) and Billy Aprahamian fires at 1/2 in the last 14 days; sits naturally just behind the leader in a prominent role and the step back up in trip from its last two runs — both placed on good — suits a horse that stays well, headgear (hood) adding a tactical focus angle.

runners_data.name: Ukantango
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners a genuine hold-up horse trained by the in-form Olly Murphy (3/16 in 14 days), and two wins include a success on soft going that underlines versatility; 54 days off the track is worth monitoring for freshness, and the tongue-tie plus cheekpieces are retained from its last run — this horse needs the pace to be honestly run and is structurally the least favoured in a potentially slow-tempo contest.

runners_data.name: Le Gentleman
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor's five-year-old is the freshest horse in the field on just 19 days since winning over course-adjacent good ground, and that recent win (2/5 on sim going) shows real relevance; Jack Tudor is a strong jockey booking and the horse's natural prominent style means it will look to push for a prominent pitch, though the field is congested at the head of affairs and it may not get as free a run as it wants.

runners_data.name: My Friend Sean
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's seven-year-old carries the lowest weight and is a natural prominent racer by preference, but recent form (6636-5) is the weakest in the field and this horse is among those squeezed out of its ideal position by the cluster of prominent types ahead of it; Stan Sheppard takes the ride and the tongue-tie and cheekpieces are retained, but until the form figures improve, it is hard to make a strong case.

races.paceDynamic: Theonlywayiswessex is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to press them, Alan King's eight-year-old can expect to control tempo from the front across this 2m4f trip at Uttoxeter. Pep Talking is a natural prominent racer and will look to sit just off the lead, likely making it a two-horse show at the head of affairs early. Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean are both genuine prominent types by preference but the field cannot accommodate three horses pressing Theonlywayiswessex, so at least one — most plausibly My Friend Sean given the lower weight and less consistent recent form — will be shuffled back from their natural position; Le Gentleman, freshest of the trio on 19 days since last run with a good recent win, has the sharpness to contest for that second slot. Ukantango settles in rear as the one true hold-up horse in the field. This race shape — a lone leader setting a measured, uncontested gallop — is a classically front-runner-friendly setup that could reward those who travel prominently and jump fluently, meaning horses able to sit on Theonlywayiswessex's quarters and strike from the front rank are best-placed; true hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage unless the pace becomes unsustainably hot, which there is little evidence to suggest it will.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Theonlywayiswessex is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a measured, jumping-fluent tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Theonlywayiswessex controls every fence from the front, and a horse sitting comfortably in second — most likely Pep Talking — can track and pounce approaching the last if the leader ties up; this scenario rewards prominent racers who jump cleanly and can sustain pressure in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Pep Talking or Le Gentleman tracks the leader relentlessly and hits the front before the last, taking the race away from Theonlywayiswessex.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third throughout picks the moment to move before two out, and the front-runner, having done all the work, cannot find an answer; this shape benefits horses with strong recent course form and good jumping at pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front two press hard enough to set a truly searching gallop and the pace blows up in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Ukantango, whose best win came from off the pace on good ground, is the only genuine hold-up horse and benefits structurally if the race becomes a true stamina test; however, Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean are not natural closers despite being mapped to midfield, meaning genuine late-running firepower is limited and this scenario carries reduced conviction.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Late
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors disrupt the front rank and multiple horses lose their rhythm in the closing stages, creating a muddled finish.
scenarios.body: A scrappy, error-ridden contest can throw the race open to any survivor who is still travelling at the second-last; in a small field of five, one clear round at the right moment could be decisive regardless of style.

watchPoints.text: Theonlywayiswessex — if it jumps cleanly from the front with no pressure, Alan King's runner could lead wire-to-wire and lap up an uncontested pace; any jumping error at a critical fence is the only real threat to this structural dominance.

Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean — both genuine prominent types who cannot all get their natural position; watch for crowding and interference in the early stages as they compete for the same real estate behind Theonlywayiswessex.

Ukantango — the only true hold-up horse needs a strong, honest gallop to close late, and if Theonlywayiswessex sets a steady tempo (which is likely unopposed), Ukantango's late run may arrive too late to win.

Pep Talking — headgear (hood) is retained and Gavin Sheehan's booking for a trainer firing at 50% in 14 days is a positive angle; watch whether Pep Talking can establish second position early and control the race from there behind the leader.

Going remains officially unknown at Uttoxeter — if the surface rides on the cut side of good, Ukantango's soft-ground wins become more relevant and the pace dynamic could loosen, benefiting hold-up horses more than currently projected.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hello Cello
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare trained by Harry Fry who stays well and has consistent good-ground form, but her six finishes from hold-up positions at this sort of trip suggest she needs a strong gallop that may not materialise here; 17 days since last run is fine, and a 7lb claimer (Ciaran O'Shea) keeps the weight manageable.

runners_data.name: Kayla's Friend
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's mare won last time out and holds a strong record on Good ground (4/5 in similar going); the STYLE_FIT flag is relevant — she is mapped prominently but is essentially the race's pace-maker, and her chance is very much tied to whether she can control from the front without being pressured.

runners_data.name: Camshaft
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. rides this five-year-old who has won twice at trip and surface combinations resembling today, and her prominent style is a natural fit for the likely race shape; only 1/5 in similar going demands a note, but her two recent wins suggest the form is there when conditions click.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Neil King's mare has been consistently placed on Good ground (four top-four finishes in last five on the surface) without winning, and Jack Quinlan rides a hold-up type who will need the pace to be strong enough over 2m7½f to generate a meaningful late run — the current race shape makes that uncertain.

runners_data.name: Grey Gamble
runners_data.note: Emma Lavelle's unbeaten-style flag runner whose recent record shows four finishes in the 4-5 bracket; an unknown style (U) means tactical flexibility exists, but no win in five similar-going runs (0W0P) is a concern and Ben Jones will need to find a favourable position early.

runners_data.name: Theirshegoes
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type who has finished 3P in good-ground races but has not won from this style tag; Joshua Thompson's 5lb claim reduces the weight, though the mare's age and lack of a win on comparable going over this sort of trip limits her claims in the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Faerie Cutlass
runners_data.note: Kim Bailey and Mat Nicholls' eight-year-old carries tongue-strap and hood and wants to race prominently, but her recent form string (U467-7) and 0W1P record on similar going over comparable trips makes her hard to trust even if she does secure a forward position off the front.

runners_data.name: Belladinotte
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's mare has a solid record at 24f on Good (two wins, multiple places) and Harry Bannister takes the ride; she maps to a prominent position which suits, and her course-trip profile is the most encouraging of the prominent pack behind Kayla's Friend — 1/3 for the trainer in the last 14 days adds a small positive flag.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: Four-year-old trained by Harriet Dickin with blinkers fitted, who has placed in three of her last four on Good ground and is lightly raced enough to be unexposed; Megan Bevan's 7lb claim is useful weight relief, and her unknown style (U) means she could slot into whichever shape develops, though the lowest weight in the field reflects her mark.

runners_data.name: Global Hideaway
runners_data.note: Christian Williams' five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type whose natural style has placed him further back in the field than the map shows — his redistribution to midfield reflects congestion at the rear, not a change in racing style; Jack Tudor is a top jockey, but 0W0P in similar going and a form string showing a pulled-up run limits confidence regardless of positioning.

races.paceDynamic: Kayla's Friend is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner mares' handicap hurdle over 2m7½f, and with no genuine challenger identified to push her early, Sean Bowen can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — a shape that suits her profile but also risks setting a tempo that keeps the field compact and in contention throughout. Camshaft and Faerie Cutlass will both want to race prominently, and Belladinotte is another who maps to a forward position, meaning Kayla's Friend will not be entirely alone up front, but she holds the clearest claim on the lead. Global Hideaway is a genuine hold-up type redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is over-subscribed with closers — the field carries more hold-up/prominent horses than can all achieve their natural positions, with Kayla's Friend and Camshaft most likely to secure the front rank. At this trip on Good ground with a single pace-setter setting a measured gallop, the race shape favours prominent racers who can settle just off the leader and conserve energy for the final climb, rather than deep closers who may find the pace insufficient to generate a meaningful late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kayla's Friend Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kayla's Friend is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip unchallenged, dictating from the front with Camshaft and Belladinotte just in behind.
scenarios.body: Bowen gets the dream lead and sets a tempo that suits his mare, while the prominent pair track without burning too much fuel; the winner is likely to emerge from the first three or four in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Camshaft and Belladinotte push up aggressively early, compressing the lead and turning it into a more genuinely contested race.
scenarios.body: A moderate-to-strong gallop develops with multiple horses racing prominently, suiting those with the class and jumping fluency to sustain their position over the final two hurdles; hold-up horses still struggle to get involved.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set too strong a pace for the trip and begin to weaken inside the final half-mile, opening the door for hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Hello Cello and Blackwater Lilly are the most credible closers in this field, and if the gallop has enough genuine quality to stretch the field, they can pick up the pieces; this shape is less likely given Global Hideaway's redistribution and the overall modest pace outlook.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Kayla's Friend is headed or jumps poorly early, causing a muddled, slow-run race with a chaotic final-hurdle scrum.
scenarios.body: A falsely-run race over this trip can produce unpredictable results with multiple horses finishing in a cluster; unexposed or lightly-raced types with tactical speed can benefit from the lottery finish.

watchPoints.text: Kayla's Friend — if Sean Bowen allows her to stride on unchallenged from flag-fall, the entire race is likely to be run at her terms; watch whether any of the prominent trio (Camshaft, Belladinotte, Faerie Cutlass) apply early pressure.

Camshaft — Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will be intent on a prominent pitch and if he pushes to go with Kayla's Friend, the early pace could be meaningfully stronger than the single-front-runner map implies, which would open the door for closers.

Athena's Dream — the four-year-old with blinkers is the least exposed horse in the field and unknown style means she could take any position; watch for Megan Bevan (7lb claim) being aggressive early to compensate for inexperience, as this could disrupt the anticipated race shape.

Global Hideaway — Jack Tudor will seek to get this hold-up type into a better position than the map suggests, but if the field is compact and the pace is controlled, he may find himself unable to make his move until the final fence; note that his true role is as a closer, not a midfield tracker.

Hello Cello — with a 7lb claimer aboard and a hold-up style, she is wholly dependent on the front-runners weakening late over 2m7½f; if Kayla's Friend coasts home, Hello Cello's chance evaporates regardless of how well she travels through the race.
